description: Exploration of the universe from solar system to cosmology

notable_moons.Titan: Saturn's largest moon; has thick atmosphere
notable_moons.Europa: Jupiter's moon; liquid ocean beneath ice crust
notable_moons.Io: Most volcanically active body in solar system

stellar_lifecycle.nebula: Cloud of gas and dust; stellar nursery
stellar_lifecycle.low_mass_end: Red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf
stellar_lifecycle.high_mass_end: Supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole

galaxy_types.spiral: Arms of stars extending from central bulge (e.g., Milky Way)
galaxy_types.elliptical: Oval-shaped, older stars, little star formation
galaxy_types.irregular: No defined shape; often result of galactic collisions

cosmology.big_bang: Universe originated ~13.8 billion years ago from an extremely hot, dense state
cosmology.cosmic_microwave_background: Afterglow of Big Bang; discovered 1965 by Penzias and Wilson
cosmology.dark_matter: Invisible mass comprising ~27% of universe; inferred from gravitational effects

black_holes.definition: Region where gravity is so strong nothing, not even light, can escape
black_holes.singularity: Point of infinite density at the center

types.stellar: Formed from collapsed massive stars (3–100 solar masses)
types.supermassive: Found at galaxy centers (millions to billions of solar masses)

black_holes.hawking_radiation: Theoretical thermal radiation emitted from black holes

space_exploration_milestones.1961: Yuri Gagarin – first human in space
space_exploration_milestones.1969: Apollo 11 – first humans on the Moon
space_exploration_milestones.2004: Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity land
space_exploration_milestones.2023: India's Chandrayaan-3 lands near lunar south pole
